analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows: After The Plunge (6 November 2026)
key_insights: DB's consolidated equity positioning measure fell to a sizable underweight (-0.54sd, 20th percentile) in one of the sharpest weekly drops on record, the biggest weekly drop since Liberation Day.

Discretionary investor positioning is at -1.07sd (3rd percentile), below the bottom of its usual band. Systematic strategies cut from well overweight to slightly above neutral (0.10sd, 44th percentile).

Large-cap positioning (-0.34sd, 24th percentile) turned underweight for the first time in seven months. DB says this is in line with zero S&P 500 earnings growth, and discretionary positioning is consistent with negative growth. For comparison, S&P 500 EPS growth was 34% in Q2 and Q3 and the median S&P 500 company grew nearly 15% in Q3.

Tech is the epicenter of the drop. MCG & large-cap Tech positioning (-0.77sd, 7th percentile) is at its lowest since April 2023, below positioning for the rest of the S&P 500 and below Liberation Day lows. DB says this matches Tech earnings growth turning negative, versus Q3 Tech growth of 53% in aggregate and 35% for the median company.
Tech relative performance broke slightly below its long-run trend channel, similar to overshoots around the start of the Iran war and Liberation Day.

DB attributes this week's selloff mainly to a forced positioning unwind. The incremental news from the mid-term elections was modest, and opposition to data centers was already seen as a bipartisan issue.
DB remains overweight Tech. It upgraded Tech back to overweight on Oct 30 after an earlier unwind, and says the plunge this week makes risk-reward even more favorable.

Equity fund inflows were $89.2bn, a 20-week high. EM took $45.1bn, its largest on record, led by China ($34.5bn) and Taiwan ($8.6bn, a record). The US took $31.7bn. Europe saw outflows for a fourth straight week.
Money market funds took $140.4bn, mostly US ($130.2bn). Bond fund inflows ($11.6bn) fell to a seven-week low, and EM bonds had their biggest outflows since May 2022 (-$6.0bn).

Systematic de-risking: vol-control funds cut equity allocation to the lowest since April (25th percentile) and are more sensitive to further selloffs. CTAs cut US equity exposure and are at their lowest equity allocation since May (47th percentile). Risk parity funds trimmed equities but remain high (83rd percentile).

Options and sentiment turned defensive. The call-to-put volume ratio fell sharply (21st percentile) and 3-month S&P 500 90%-110% skew hit a seven-month high. AAII bull-minus-bear spread dropped to the most bearish in six weeks (13th percentile). The most-shorted stocks and the highest net call volume baskets underperformed.
Sector positioning is mixed. Consumer Cyclicals, Industrial Cyclicals, Real Estate, Staples and Utilities fell deep into underweight. Energy (0.12sd) and Healthcare (0.15sd) are slightly overweight.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning has fallen to the bottom of its historical band and is consistent with negative Tech earnings growth. DB says the unwind makes risk-reward even more favorable.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 EPS growth was 34% y/y in Q2 and about 34% in Q3 (Q3 labelled blended in DB's chart, so not all companies had reported). The median S&P 500 company grew nearly 15% in Q3.
Tech Q3 EPS growth was 53% in aggregate and 35% for the median company. DB says Tech positioning now matches negative Tech earnings growth and large estimate cuts.

DB says large-cap equity positioning matches zero S&P 500 earnings growth and is factoring in large outright estimate cuts. These are DB's inferences from positioning, not forecasts of actual earnings.
DB's own S&P 500 EPS forecasts are $358 for 2026 and $420 for 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Technology (sector allocation call), upgraded back to overweight on Oct 30 2026 and reiterated Nov 6
trade_ideas.rationale: The unwind in relative performance and positioning has made risk-reward favorable, and the plunge this week makes it even more favorable.

risk_factors: Further selling by vol-control funds, whose sensitivity to additional selloffs has increased.
Investors view the current earnings growth boom as narrow and unsustainable.
Tech relative performance has broken below its long-run trend channel.
Discretionary positioning is at the bottom of its historical band, and CTAs were cut significantly in US equities.
EM bonds had their largest outflows since May 2022.
charts_described: Consolidated equity positioning chart shows the current reading at the 20th percentile since 2010.
Discretionary vs systematic positioning chart shows discretionary at the 3rd percentile and systematic at the 44th.
Large-cap equity positioning vs S&P 500 EPS growth chart cites a correlation of 39% since 2012, with the Q3 median growth marked.
Tech positioning vs earnings growth chart cites a correlation of 54% since 2011.
S&P 500 ratio to its 1-year moving average vs EPS growth chart cites a correlation of 56% for 1995-2017.
Tech relative performance chart shows a trend growth of 14.2% annualized since 2016 with a +/-10% band, and a break below the band.
Systematic strategies positioning vs S&P 500 realized volatility cites a correlation of -77%.
Discretionary positioning vs ISM Manufacturing cites a correlation of 67%, and vs S&P 500 EPS growth a correlation of 50% since 2010.
vol_and_positioning: Consolidated equity positioning is -0.54sd (20th percentile). Discretionary is -1.07sd (3rd percentile). Systematic is 0.10sd (44th percentile).
Large caps are at -0.34sd (24th percentile), MCG & Tech at -0.77sd (7th percentile) and small caps at -0.66sd (18th percentile).
Vol-control funds are at the 25th percentile of equity allocation, the lowest since April, with increased sensitivity to further selloffs.

CTAs: equity allocation is at the 47th percentile. US is at the 27th percentile, Nasdaq 100 24th, Russell 2000 22nd, Europe 57th, Japan 33rd and EM 34th. Dollar longs are at the 92nd percentile, copper longs 91st, oil longs 76th and gold shorts 24th.
Risk parity equity allocation is at the 83rd percentile (US 87th). Commodity allocation is at the 99th percentile.
S&P 500 3-month 90%-110% skew surged to the highest in seven months. The call-to-put volume ratio fell to the 21st percentile.
AAII bearish responses are at the 94th percentile, a seven-week high. The bull-minus-bear spread is at the 13th percentile.
Net call volume fell broadly across single stocks, index and ETF options. The basket of stocks with the most net call volume the prior week and the most-shorted basket both underperformed.
Equity long/short hedge fund 1-month beta to the S&P 500 is at the 79th percentile and 3-month beta at the 84th percentile.
geopolitical: US mid-term elections (blue sweep) on Tuesday. DB says attention has focused on it as the selloff driver, but the incremental news was modest.
Opposition to data centers is described as a large bipartisan issue that was widely acknowledged before the elections.
The Iran war and Liberation Day are cited as earlier episodes when Tech relative performance overshot its trend channel.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning now matches zero S&P 500 earnings growth and negative Tech growth, well below actual Q3 growth (34% for the S&P 500, nearly 15% for the median company, 53% aggregate and 35% median for Tech). DB says this makes risk-reward in Tech favorable.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors clearly view the current earnings growth boom as narrow and unsustainable, and DB asks where the line should be drawn. Vol-control and CTA selling and the break in Tech relative performance below its trend channel could extend the unwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings growth actually turning negative (zero for the S&P 500, negative for Tech), the level at which positioning now sits.
